item.title: Researchers develop AI-generated videos designed to maximally stimulate specific brain regions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have created AI-generated videos aimed at maximally activating targeted brain regions. This approach uses artificial intelligence to tailor visual stimuli that can influence neural activity in precise areas of the brain. The project explores the intersection of AI and neuroscience to better understand and potentially manipulate brain function through customized video content.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 family with flagship Sol model offering improved intelligence, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness across coding, knowledge work, and science [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: OpenAI has released the GPT-5.6 family of models, including the flagship Sol, Terra, and Luna variants, designed to deliver more intelligence per token and stronger performance per dollar. GPT-5.6 Sol achieves state-of-the-art results in coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and scientific tasks while reducing token usage and estimated costs compared to previous models and competitors. The release also introduces an ultra setting that coordinates multiple agents to accelerate complex workflows. The models underwent extensive evaluation and red teaming to enhance safeguards against misuse without limiting legitimate applications. GPT-5.6 Sol sets new benchmarks on professional workflow evaluations and coding agent indexes, outperforming competitors like Claude Fable 5 at significantly lower costs and faster completion times. The family includes efficient smaller models, Terra and Luna, which offer affordable intelligence for everyday tasks. The update also features Programmatic Tool Calling to improve tool-heavy task coordination and flexible performance settings to balance efficiency and capability.

item.title: Meta launches Muse Spark 1.1 multimodal reasoning model with improved agentic tasks, coding, and tool use, available via new Meta Model API [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs introduced Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded multimodal reasoning model designed for agentic tasks including planning, coding, and multimodal understanding. The model supports complex workflows across multiple applications, manages a large context window, and improves performance on coding tasks such as debugging and feature implementation. Muse Spark 1.1 is accessible through the new Meta Model API and integrated into the Meta AI app and meta.ai for public preview. The model advances Meta's vision of personal superintelligence by enabling efficient orchestration of multi-agent systems, adapting to evolving task requirements, and combining perception with action in real-world scenarios. It demonstrates significant gains over its predecessor in speed and capability, supporting diverse use cases from automated coding to multimodal interaction with visual and audio inputs. Researchers and developers at Meta are already leveraging Muse Spark 1.1 to enhance productivity and automate model development workflows.

item.title: Developers build a real-time AI tutor for children aged 4-9 with sub-second response times to maintain engagement and effective teaching [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A team has developed an AI tutor designed to teach math and reading to children aged 4 to 9, focusing on real-time interaction with sub-second response times to keep young learners engaged. The system departs from standard AI agent loops by streaming multiple actions in a single response, allowing immediate execution of teaching steps without long pauses that can cause children to lose attention. The developers emphasized embedding pedagogy into the AI's architecture, balancing instruction quality and latency. They created a custom harness to manage action generation and execution separately, enabling the tutor to adapt its teaching approach dynamically and validate actions without interrupting the flow. This approach aims to replicate the responsiveness and adaptability of human teachers in a digital format.

item.title: Deutsche Telekom integrates AI across customer service, employee workflows, and network operations to become an AI-native telecommunications company [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Deutsche Telekom is transforming its telecommunications operations by embedding AI into customer service, employee workflows, and network management, aiming to become one of the first AI-native telcos. The company serves over 300 million customers and has seen a 546% increase in AI tool usage since early 2026, with more than 50,000 monthly active users of ChatGPT and related APIs. The transformation involves redesigning workflows rather than simply adding AI tools, with initiatives including AI-powered customer care, real-time network optimization, and innovations in voice communications such as live translation and intelligent call assistance. Deutsche Telekom collaborates with OpenAI and other partners to integrate AI directly into everyday communication channels, enhancing customer interactions without requiring new applications. This approach reflects a broader strategy to democratize AI access and embed intelligence into existing telecommunications infrastructure, focusing on operational redesign and balancing leadership direction with employee experimentation to drive adoption and process change.

item.description: wpconverters.com has introduced an interactive tool that allows users to drag boxes around a canvas and watch a layout engine infer the corresponding Flexbox layout in real time without relying on AI. The tool supports multi-selection, group movement, resizing, alignment, and removal of elements through intuitive mouse controls. This playground offers a hands-on way to understand Flexbox behavior by manipulating visual elements directly.

He also plans to allocate some of his personal shares to employee incentives as part of this commitment.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang links engineer retention to AI token usage relative to salary amid $2 billion annual token budget [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang revealed on the All-In Podcast at GTC 2026 that he evaluates engineers based on their AI token consumption compared to their salary, expressing concern if a $500,000 engineer uses less than half that amount in tokens annually. Nvidia is targeting a $2 billion yearly token expenditure for its engineering team, reflecting a broader industry trend where companies shift spending from payroll to AI token costs. Huang's approach highlights efforts to manage AI-related expenses without reducing workforce size, emphasizing efficiency in token usage as a key factor in retaining talent.

item.title: Refik Anadol's Dataland opens as world's first AI art museum with immersive rainforest exhibit using wearables and AI-trained on Amazon data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Dataland, co-founded by artist Refik Anadol in downtown Los Angeles, launched as the world's first museum dedicated to AI art, featuring an immersive exhibit called Machine Dreams: Rainforest. The exhibit uses wearable devices to track visitors' biometrics and movements, generating dynamic digital visuals and soundscapes based on AI models trained with extensive natural science data collected from the Amazon and other rainforests. Anadol and his team spent three years developing their own AI models using five petabytes of data sourced with researcher consent, aiming to create an ethical and environmentally responsible AI art experience. The exhibit responds interactively to visitors, incorporating scents and visual effects that simulate natural environments, challenging common perceptions of AI-generated art as simplistic or derivative.

item.title: Open Science Desktop launches as an open-source, local-first AI research workbench for macOS, Windows, and Linux, offering a model-agnostic alternative to OpenAI Codex [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Open Science Desktop is a new open-source desktop application designed to run AI research workflows locally on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It provides a model-agnostic environment that supports autonomous research agents, traceable artifacts, and reproducible scientific workflows without relying on cloud services, aiming to give developers more control over their data and coding environment. The platform integrates literature search, experiment code, analysis, and report writing into one continuous session, with all outputs linked back to their source code and inputs. It supports multiple scientific data connectors and allows users to bring their own AI models, emphasizing privacy and extensibility through pluggable components and skills.

item.title: Study finds 35% of new websites by mid-2025 contain AI-generated or AI-assisted text, with increased semantic similarity but no clear drop in factual accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers from Imperial College London, Internet Archive, and Stanford University analyzed a representative sample of websites from 2022 to 2025 and found that about 35% of newly published sites were AI-generated or AI-assisted by mid-2025, up from zero before ChatGPT's launch. The study observed a rise in semantic similarity and positive sentiment in AI-generated content but did not find significant evidence of decreased factual accuracy or stylistic diversity. Public perception of AI's impact on internet content diverges from these findings. The research used multiple AI detection methods and surveyed US adults on their views and usage of AI tools to assess the broader effects of AI-generated text on online discourse.

item.title: Muscula launches AI-assisted error tracking and debugging platform integrating with major coding tools and supporting multiple programming languages [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Muscula offers a platform that uses AI to detect, explain, and fix software errors directly in the developer's terminal, eliminating the need for manual log analysis. It supports multiple languages including JavaScript, PHP, C#, and Java, and integrates with popular AI coding assistants and editors such as Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and GitHub Copilot. The platform provides real-time error alerts, prioritizes issues by severity, and includes features like uptime monitoring, team collaboration, and enterprise-grade security with GDPR compliance and self-hosting options.

item.title: DeepSWE releases benchmark results for GPT 5.6, evaluating software engineering capabilities across diverse, contamination-free tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: DeepSWE published benchmark results for GPT 5.6, using a long-horizon software engineering benchmark designed to differentiate top coding models. The benchmark features contamination-free tasks created from scratch, high diversity across 91 repositories and five programming languages, and real-world complexity requiring significantly more code and output tokens than previous benchmarks. Verification relies on hand-written tests focusing on software behavior rather than implementation details. The benchmark includes tasks such as aborting pending body reads on shutdown, fixing PromQL label sorting, adding config file parsing to commands, and generating Wasm coredumps on traps. DeepSWE aims to provide a more accurate reflection of how frontier coding agents perform in real software engineering work and updates its leaderboard as new models are released.

item.title: Datadog used Claude and Cursor AI models for test-driven migration of Stream Router from FoundationDB to PostgreSQL, cutting operation times from 45 minutes to one second and reducing database costs by 90% [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Datadog engineer Arnold Wakim detailed how the company leveraged AI tools Claude and Cursor to refactor a critical production system's storage backend, overcoming transaction size limits and improving performance. The migration involved redesigning the schema to use foreign keys and running parallel instances of the old and new systems with comprehensive testing to ensure correctness. The process included three phases: describing function intent with Claude, fixing failing tests through focused prompts, and deploying via a blue/green approach with continuous validation. While AI accelerated code generation, human input was needed for query optimizations and managing high token consumption. The migration reduced operation times from 45 minutes to about one second, cut data storage by up to 40 times, and lowered CPU, memory, and database costs significantly. Wakim emphasized that a strong test suite was crucial for trusting AI-generated code during the migration.

item.title: Ethereum Foundation's Protocol Security team runs coordinated AI agents to find bugs in protocol code, revealing challenges in triaging real issues from false positives [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The Ethereum Foundation's Protocol Security team has been using coordinated AI agents to audit critical protocol code, including systems software and cryptographic components, uncovering real bugs such as a remotely-triggerable panic in libp2p's gossipsub. The team emphasizes that the main challenge is not finding potential bugs but distinguishing true vulnerabilities from false positives through rigorous triage and reproducible proof-of-concept artifacts. The agents operate in parallel without a central coordinator, sharing findings through version control and following a structured workflow involving reconnaissance, hunting, gap-filling, and validation. Each candidate bug must include a testable claim, a clear mechanism of failure, and a self-contained reproducer that runs against the real code to be considered a valid finding. This approach aligns with similar efforts by other organizations like Anthropic and Cloudflare, highlighting a growing methodology for AI-driven security audits.

item.title: CorvinOS launches self-hosted AI agent operating system with built-in EU compliance and hash-chained audit trails [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: CorvinOS is a self-hosted operating system designed to run AI agents with compliance mechanisms integrated directly into its architecture. It features a chat-based shell interface accessible via messaging apps, local speech transcription, and structural compliance controls such as bot disclosure, consent gates, data residency enforcement, and tamper-evident audit logs. The system supports adaptive agentic compute that iterates tasks until satisfactory results are achieved, enabling complex workflows like model tuning and large dataset analysis without exposing raw data. Users can export complete workflows as portable packages for repeatable execution, ensuring data privacy and regulatory adherence throughout AI operations.

item.title: OpenAI's No. 2 executive Fidji Simo steps down from full-time role after extended medical leave, shifting to part-time advisory position amid company's IPO plans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Fidji Simo, OpenAI's chief of Applications and second-in-command, is stepping down from her full-time role due to a prolonged medical leave and will transition to a part-time advisory position. Her departure creates a leadership gap as OpenAI prepares for a potential IPO and intensifies competition with Anthropic in the enterprise AI market. Simo joined OpenAI in 2025 after leading Instacart through its IPO and previously working at Meta. She oversaw business and product operations, with key executives reporting to her. Her health issues, disclosed in April, led to other executive changes, including departures and role shifts. OpenAI recently launched new GPT-5.6 models and a productivity-focused AI agent, signaling a strategic push amid market challenges. Her exit leaves OpenAI's executive team lean during a critical growth phase, with speculation that Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser may assume greater responsibilities. The company has also adjusted employee equity vesting policies to retain talent amid an escalating AI talent war, reflecting broader organizational shifts alongside Simo's departure.

item.title: Asteroids launches managed long-horizon AI agents with omnichannel access, model and harness flexibility, and free parked agents starting at $3/month [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Asteroids has introduced a managed service for long-running AI agents that can be accessed across multiple channels with persistent history, tools, and state. Users can launch agents with one click, choose any supported harness or model, and benefit from features like snapshots, backups, secure sandboxes, and customizable tools without setup or lock-in. The platform supports continuous agent operation for months, allowing users to scale or park agents for free when idle. Built-in capabilities include image and video generation, CRM, email, social listening, scraping, and knowledge management, all accessible via a command-line interface for fleet management. Asteroids emphasizes user control by enabling model and harness swaps while preserving agent history.

Like SpaceX, Meta claimed its new model delivers performance comparable to that of established models from AI labs such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. What may be most significant, however, is Meta's apparent intention to spend a fortune subsidizing usage of its new model in hopes of pulling market share from its rivals. In an interview with Bloomberg, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta's pricing for what users would pay to use the models would be "very aggressive and attractive." item.title: Universities Fret as Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and DeepMind Lure Their Professors [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Renowned university professors and academic researchers keep joining frontier AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Remaining faculty say the brain drain is threatening the development of open source AI models in the West. So far this year, at least 22 professors and researchers have taken leave or stepped back from their roles at Stanford, Berkeley, Harvard, Virginia and the University of Southern California to work at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta Platforms, according to a review of college websites, X posts and LinkedIn profiles. The actual number of departures could be far higher, according to my conversations with professors at some of the universities. Many of the professors are computer scientists, but some are physicists, economists, statisticians or mathematicians. Two of them taught philosophy, which probably has something to do with the philosophical questions that arise when labs shape the personalities and self-awareness of AI. (See the list below.) Just last week, Jelani Nelson, the chair of Berkeley's department of electrical engineering and computer science, and UT Austin philosophy professor Harvey Lederman said they'd be taking leave to join Anthropic as members of its technical staff. (Lederman will continue teaching at New York University.) AI professors have been leaving school for big jobs at Google and its ilk since deep learning and self-driving software got hot 15 years ago, and after the generative AI boom got rolling a couple of years ago. But Berkeley computer science professor and AI researcher Joey Gonzalez said the exits have accelerated this year. The reason is the same as it's always been: It's simply more difficult to do cutting edge research in academia because it requires large amounts of expensive AI servers, which the schools generally don't have. Chart by Shane Burke.

item.title: Khosla-Backed Startup Claims Breakthrough With Largest-Ever AI Model on an iPhone [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Apple is on a quest to shrink powerful AI models to run on iPhones, which could cut down on cloud computing costs and enhance user privacy. But a small startup that emerged from stealth mode earlier this year says it recently got an AI model running on an iPhone bigger than any previous mobile model. The startup, PrismML, said it has shrunk down Qwen 3.6, an open-source large language model developed by Chinese internet giant Alibaba, to run on an iPhone 17 Pro. The model has 27 billion parameters, which are roughly similar to the synapses in a brain and can help determine the complexity of the data a model can process. In contrast, most models that run on mobile phones have only a few billion parameters active at a time.

item.title: OpenAI pairs its GPT-5.6 public rollout with ChatGPT Work, a new agent that handles entire workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI is launching ChatGPT Work, an agent-based product powered by Codex and the now publicly available GPT-5.6. The agent can independently handle complex projects across apps like Google Drive, Slack, and Salesforce. ChatGPT Work is available now on web, mobile, and desktop, though access depends on the subscription plan. item.description: Meta is entering the AI API business with Muse Spark 1.1 at prices that undercut even the dirt-cheap Grok 4.5, released just yesterday.
